items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We also had engaged a male singer this time to make the tour... This fellow's name was Tommy Brookins

ctx.x: I closed at the Faun the 30th of September and arrived in Paris the 2nd of October. I had been in touch with the trombone player Bill Tamper, whom I had toured with a few days on another occasion, and I had signed Bill for my coming tour to replace Herman Wilson who had stayed in Germany with Donald Brown. Bishop and Eddy de Hass, who later changed his namee for Eddie O'Hare, arrived in Paris about the same time as I. We also had engaged a male singer this time to make the tour as there were no girl…

After seven good rehearsals, we had a very nice repertoire. We accompanied Tommy on three numbers and he did one at the piano which was "black coffee" and I liked this number better than any of the others he did. I don't remember what Tommy had been doing in Europe and I don't remember how I happened to get in touch with him, maybe through Bish. He had a big Cadillac car and a fine blonde Swedish chick. He was going to make the tour in his car which was almost as big as the bus we had for the band, and he has to…

Most of my rehearsals taken place in the celler studio where the "Jazz Hot Magazine" run by Charles Delaunay had it's office on rue Chaptal, and I was never obliged to pay for the use of the studio and I shall always be grateful for that. And this time, I did not volunteer to pay the musicians for rehearsals, as I did when preparing for my first tour, which gesture was not appreciated by most of the guys. But I kept the rule of paying a half day salary if we had any days off.
